newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat says Israel play-acting at peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Israel play-acting at peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Saturday complained to an emergency Arab League meeting that Israel was only play-acting at peace and was not serious in implementing agreements it had made with him.

"There is an impasse not only on the Palestinian track but the Syrian and Lebanese tracks, where nothing has been implemeted concerning the agreements signed and agreed upon," Arafat told reporters at the end of the meeting.

"There is an attempt only to make a political show, to give the impression that there is a tendency from the Israelis to move in an accurate way, while on the ground there is nothing concrete in our hands," he added.
Arafat requested the extraordinary Arab League meeting to air his grievances against the right-wing Israeli government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu which came to power after elections in May.
"This was an important opportunity to put my Arab brothers in the picture regarding the dangerous circumstances that we are going through and that directly affect the peace process," Arafat said.

"I also told them about attempts by Israel to freeze implementation of what was agreed upon and its (Israel's) making do with meetings that only have a political facade. This puts the peace process in real danger."

In public speeches before the closed session requested by Arafat, Arab foreign ministers deplored Israel's new attitude towards peace talks and said it had violated or reneged on agreements made by the previous government.
"Israel bears full responsibility for the setbacks and the stalemate through its attitude of arrogance, obstinacy and provocation," said Algeria's Ahmed Attaf.
"For the principle of land for peace, it has substituted the principle of land and peace for Israel in exchange for a fragile peace for the Arabs. We must stand up to this," he added.

Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel-Meguid, in a speech prepared for the closed session with Arafat, said Israeli practices broke all the rules and principles of international law, as well as agreements made by the previous government.
